analysis:
All three changed files are test-only: MockCoordinator.swift adds a pushPrefetchModel helper (a mock-side coordinator frame sender), OperatorModelFilterTests.swift is new, and ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift is adjusted. No production source is visible in this batch, so there is no direct change to authentication, attestation, encryption, key custody, or cache storage.

The tests assert that the provider's operator-selected enabled-model filter (BackendSettings.enabledModels) refuses coordinator-driven desired_models successors, prefetch_model, and load_model for builds the operator deselected. Refusal shows up as a model_not_selected error, no prefetch starts, nothing is added to ordinarily served or advertised models, and no cache directory is created. These cover availability, integrity and weight-download controls: A-004, A-018, T-012, T-027, and TB-002 coordinator-to-provider trust (a coordinator-pushed model is not trusted beyond operator selection). In ProviderModelSwitchTests, the deselected alias successor is not prefetched and desiredSwapDrop stays empty after a switch, while an in-selection build still converges.

The MockCoordinator regression trap for /v1/telemetry/events records any telemetry POST, which is privacy-positive. No test weakening was found. The PR's production filter implementation is not in the supplied units, so the actual enforcement code (the ProviderLoop handlers for load, prefetch, reconcileDesiredModels, and applyModelSelection) must be verified in another batch. Remaining integration question: do the production handlers enforce the filter on every path (reconnect, switch, autopilot, startup preload)? The tests suggest yes, but the source is not visible here.
